## The bridge is DELIBERATELY paused — this alarm is expected, not a new fault

`reconcile-bridge.yml` is currently `disabled_manually` by operator decision. **This canary will
keep firing, and keep rotating a fresh ticket each cycle, until the bridge is re-enabled.** Each
new canary ticket will look like an unexplained P1 unless someone reads this, so the context is
repeated here rather than left on the closed predecessor (`grievous-vulgar-sanderling`).

### Why it was paused

The bridge was failing every hourly run AND re-posting ~205 duplicate comments per pass across
~28 Jira issues (~4,920/day). It was net-negative: sync was already failing, while the duplicates
it posted are durable and need manual cleanup.

### Root cause — CONFIRMED, fix in review

`irongrey-chubby-oxpecker` (`aa7b-5e47-6d3d-4615`, P1). The PRIMARY comment-dedup skip
`binding_store.is_comment_mapped(local_comment_key)` was inert in production because the
`comment_ids` map was empty (`bindings: 2475` / `comment_ids: 0`), leaving only a lossy
body-equality fallback that never matches richly-formatted comments.

Proven at runtime: **guard 3** (`if not comment_id: return` in `_record_comment_id`). On the
Cloud/ACLI transport `add_comment` returns ACLI's batch mutation envelope, not a comment
resource — a live non-mutating probe returned `{"results":[{...,"id":"ZZNOPE-424242"}],...}`
where `results[].id` is the **work item key**, never a comment id. So no id was ever recorded and
the dedup map shipped empty from day one. Fix is Gerrit **1957**.

### Before re-enabling

1. 1957 lands (`LLM-Review +1`; awaiting `Verified`).
2. The already-posted duplicates are remediated, following the `bd80-0603-7d44-4d9f` precedent —
   in progress.
3. `gh workflow enable reconcile-bridge.yml` — an explicit operator decision, not an automatic
   consequence of the fix landing.

The canary was deliberately left ENABLED rather than paused alongside the bridge, so that a
standing P1 remains visible as a reminder that the bridge is down. Silencing both would make it
easy to forget the bridge is off.

Follow-up `marshy-chummy-coot` (`2399-5e49-6b28-4d59`) tracks root-causing how the defect
escaped review, tests and CI.
